name: Gobi Gurvan Saikhan National Park
blurb: Saxaul, ibex and argali, and the snow leopards and wolves that hunt them.

tip.title: Thin the ibex
tip.text: Siberian ibex are a main prey of snow leopards. Set Siberian ibex to -80% and watch snow leopards, wolves, foxes and ravens, and then the argali they turn to.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.name: Black saxaul
nodes.desc: A tough desert shrub or small tree of loose sand. In the Gobi it is often the only tree, and its roots help hold dunes in place.

nodes.name: Siberian nitraria
nodes.desc: A salt-tolerant spiny shrub of sandy hollows and dune edges, recorded often in the park area.

nodes.name: Needlegrasses
nodes.desc: Low, drought-hardy bunch grasses are among the main plants of the Gobi, grazed by wild and domestic hoofed animals.

nodes.name: Goitered gazelle
nodes.desc: A slender gazelle of open gravel plains and desert, and one of the most-recorded large herbivores near the park.

nodes.name: Siberian ibex
nodes.desc: A mountain goat of the rocky ranges and a main prey of snow leopards in Mongolia.

nodes.name: Argali
nodes.desc: The largest wild sheep. It grazes grasses, sedges and shrubs on mountain slopes, and wolves and snow leopards hunt it.

nodes.name: Asiatic wild ass
nodes.desc: A fast grazing equid of the open Gobi plains that roams long distances to find forage and water.

nodes.name: Wild Bactrian camel
nodes.desc: A critically endangered camel of the Gobi that survives on sparse desert plants and can drink salty water.

nodes.name: Northern three-toed jerboa
nodes.desc: A small hopping rodent of sandy ground that shelters in burrows. Foxes, shrikes and snakes take it.

nodes.name: Pallas's pika
nodes.desc: A small herbivore of rocky ground, among the most-recorded mammals near the park and food for small carnivores.

nodes.name: Tolai hare
nodes.desc: A hare of steppe and semi-desert that feeds on grasses and shrubs and is prey for foxes and wolves.

nodes.name: Gobi bear
nodes.desc: A rare brown bear living near desert oases. It eats mostly plants and roots, with a little animal food such as rodents.

nodes.name: Red fox
nodes.desc: An adaptable hunter of small mammals and reptiles that also feeds on carcasses.

nodes.name: Pallas's cat
nodes.desc: A small, stocky wild cat of rocky steppe and desert that hunts pikas and small rodents.

nodes.name: Great grey shrike
nodes.desc: A predatory songbird that takes small rodents, birds and large insects, and impales prey on thorns.

nodes.name: Common raven
nodes.desc: A clever scavenger that cleans up carcasses left by larger predators and also hunts small prey.

nodes.name: Snow leopard
nodes.desc: The mountain apex predator of the Gobi ranges. Ibex and argali are its main prey in Mongolia.

nodes.name: Grey wolf
nodes.desc: Wolves hunt argali, ibex, gazelles and other hoofed animals across the Gobi, and visit the park from its surroundings.

nodes.name: Summer rain
nodes.desc: Most of the Gobi's small yearly rainfall comes in summer, setting how much grass and shrub can grow.

nodes.name: Oasis springs
nodes.desc: Scattered springs and seeps are the water that desert plants, wild asses, camels and bears gather around.

nodes.name: Snow and ice melt
nodes.desc: Winter snow and the ice field of Yolyn Am feed meltwater into the mountain valleys and the dry plains below.

nodes.name: Sandy soil
nodes.desc: Loose sand and gravel soils are poor in nutrients; dead matter returning to them is what lets plants grow.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Fungi, bacteria and insects break down dead plants and carcasses and return nutrients to the soil.
